item.title: The lighthouse keepers who timed fog signals by counting their own breath
item.description: Before clockwork, keepers at remote lighthouses spaced fog signals by counting breaths. The method was imprecise but needed no equipment and could not break, a reliability bought by giving up exact timing.

item.title: A village where every roof drains into one shared cistern
item.description: In a dry mountain village, roofs are tilted so that rain from every house flows into a single communal cistern. No one manages the water; the slope does. The cost is that one broken gutter affects everyone downstream.
